court: Lehigh County Court of Common Pleas
holding_summary: The court affirmed a zoning board's denial of an application to convert a residence into a two-unit apartment for six unrelated male tenants, holding the ordinance's restrictive definition of 'family' (excluding unrelated groups) was constitutional under the police power and citing Village of Belle Terre's rationale that boarding-house-type occupancy causes crowding, parking, and noise problems in residential neighborhoods.

quotes.text: The regimes of boarding houses, fraternity houses, and the like present urban problems. More people occupy a given space; more cars rather continuously pass by; more cars are parked; noise travels with crowds.

The board, following a hearing, observed that the premises have in fact been used as a boarding house for several years without requisite approval and concluded that a continuation of the present manner of operation of the premises would be detrimental to the neighborhood by reason of nuisance characteristics which arose from the overuse of the property.

Now, May 9, 1975, it is ordered that the appeal of Louis W. and Mattie T. Humphrey from the decision of the zoning hearing board of the City of Allentown be and the same is hereby dismissed and the decision is affirmed.

notes: Premises had operated as an unapproved boarding house for years; court sustains restrictive family-based zoning against unrelated-tenant occupancy, quoting Belle Terre's boarding-house rationale.

court: Lehigh County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Zoning dispute over classifying a manufactured home as a mobile home vs. sectional ranch house; unrelated to lodging.

court: Columbia County Court of Common Pleas
holding_summary: The court affirmed a zoning board's determination that groups of unrelated tenants renting a dwelling and its attached apartment -- each individually paying rent under a combined lease, without a common head of household -- did not qualify as a 'family' or 'household' under the residential zoning ordinance, upholding the restriction as a valid means of controlling population density.

quotes.text: If the authors of the township zoning ordinance had intended to permit groups of unrelated individuals to live together in an R-S district, we must assume that those authors would have so indicated that intent by defining “family” as a “housekeeping unit” or a “collective domestic body.”
that each group of tenants has a single combined lease with the landlord, but that each tenant is nonetheless individually responsible for paying his own rent;
the within appeal is denied, and the decision of the Zoning Hearing Board of Scott Township is affirmed.

notes: Landlord rented to two groups of unrelated tenants who individually paid rent; court's 'household/common head' test excludes this group-tenancy arrangement from protected family status, sustaining the density-control ordinance.

court: Disciplinary Board of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania
notes: Zoning/liquor-preemption dispute over municipal regulation of 'cabaret' entertainment at licensed restaurants; unrelated to lodging.
Liquor-license transfer dispute concerning proximity of licensed premises to gasoline pumps; unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: The court affirmed denial of homeowners' application to rent their residence to a caterer for weddings and private events, holding that use was an impermissible commercial use not accessory to their residential occupancy, while the ordinance separately lists bed-and-breakfast establishments as a permitted residential use and the court noted that hosting events incidental to one's own residential use (or a tenant's) remains lawful.

quotes.text: We acknowledge that opening one’s home for events (i.e., weddings, birthdays, fundraisers, etc.) is consistent and thus customarily incidental to a residential use.
the order of the Court of Common Pleas of Delaware County is hereby AFFIRMED.

notes: Mixed: ordinance affirmatively lists bed-and-breakfast (short-term paid lodging) as a permitted residential use, but the court denies the homeowners' broader commercial catered-events venue as not accessory to residential use; B&B legality itself was not litigated on the merits.
